images.title: Seven half sheets
images.purpose: Pose the question of how many whole sheets seven half sheets make, with the cue that two halves join into one whole sheet.
images.composition: One row of seven equal half sheets across the frame, the first two pushed together and outlined, and one question below.
images.exact_structure: Exactly 7 identical half sheets of chart paper, drawn as flat upright rectangles, filled teal #0072B2. The first 2 touch along one long edge to form one whole sheet, outlined in reddish purple #CC79A7. The other 5 stand evenly spaced after a small gap, not grouped. A whole sheet is exactly twice the width of a half sheet. Below, one question line. Exactly 7 half sheets, 1 outlined pair.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more than one pair grouped or outlined, or any count of whole sheets written
images.takeaway: Every two halves make one whole sheet, so pair them up and count.
images.description: Seven equal half sheets in a row; the first two join into one whole sheet with 1/2 + 1/2 = 1, and the question asks how many whole sheets all seven make.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to keep pairing the loose halves the same way and count the pairs.

image_decisions.why: Seven equal halves with one pair joined gives the pairing cue without showing the result.
